## PART I — CHILD-VICTIM DETAIL (handle first, apply together, before anything else)

Both lenses converged here independently and neither can be deferred. These are the only two passages in the file that describe the material or identify those depicted.

### A1. §2.1, line 77 — the claimed-depiction clause. **REMOVE ENTIRELY. Highest priority in the file.**

> **Verbatim (redacted):** `"Charging documents state he represented some images as [CLAIMED DEPICTION WITHHELD — line 77]."`
> **Deletion boundary:** the entire sentence beginning `Charging documents state he represented` through the following period. Nothing of it survives.

**Public question: NONE, and the clause is indefensible on either branch.** It identifies specific children by a claimed relationship to a man named in the file's title — identifying information in exactly the way an address is — and because the file's own wording is *"represented … as,"* the truth of the claim is nowhere established: if false, the library has published a grave falsehood about real children; if true, it has published identifying detail about child victims.

**Merge note — the structural trap, stated plainly because it is the one that could talk an editor out of the removal:** recording-layer fidelity is **not** a licence to include. The two-layer rule governs **accuracy** — whether a claim is reported faithfully. The living-persons rule governs **inclusion** — whether it belongs in the file at all. This passage is perfectly faithful to the charging document and still fails the inclusion test.

**Steelman, considered and rejected:** a false representation would go to Zinn's credibility (§4, §5). Rejected — his credibility is already carried overwhelmingly by the established central fact that he falsely confessed to a murder, plus his allocution at §3.3. The marginal gain is near zero and is purchased with the identification of child victims.

### A2. §2.1, line 77 — quantity, ages, and characterisation of the material. **REMOVE; retain only the bare fact of sharing.**

> **Verbatim (redacted):** `"reported finding more than [COUNT] images of children approximately [AGE RANGE WITHHELD] in [DESCRIPTOR WITHHELD] contexts, plus [DESCRIPTOR WITHHELD] text threads in which Zinn shared images with others"`

**Public question: NONE for the quantity, ages and descriptors** — no proposition in this file and no register entry D1–D5 is weakened by their absence. **PARTIAL for the sharing**, which is conduct of the convicted subject going to the offence category (distribution as against possession) and reproduces no victim detail.

**⚖ Lens conflict resolved.** Lens A removed the whole clause; Lens B split it and kept the sharing. **Lens B's split is adopted** — it satisfies Lens A's concern completely (every victim-facing element goes) while preserving a fact about the convicted subject's own conduct. **But Lens B's stated rationale is trimmed:** the claim that distribution "is why the counts took the shape they did, which feeds D1" is itself an untested inference that the file nowhere establishes, and it must **not** be written into the file. The sharing survives on the narrower ground stated above.

**Public question: NONE.** The proposition the file needs — that at least two people were detained on 2025-09-10 and both were cleared — is what holds the Q-40 gate open, and it carries its entire evidentiary load without the name; the man is a private individual, not a party to *State v. Robinson*, not a party to Zinn's separate prosecution, not a claimant, not an official, and not alleged by anyone to have done anything.

**⚖ Lens boundary resolved, not a conflict.** The zinn-himself lens expressly declined to adjudicate this as another lens's item and warned that its absence from that list must not be read as clearance. It is adjudicated here.

**Three points make removal urgent rather than merely permitted:**

1. **INFLATED TIER.** The sentence is marked **[T2]**, but both cited sources are **T3** journalism (NewsNation, Newsweek), *and the DPS attribution itself is carried only by that T3 reporting.* The library's actual Tier 2 holding — the same-day 2025-09-10 press conference, read directly — does not name him. My corpus re-run (both U+FFFE readings, BAM excluded, positive control passing) confirms no banked artifact names him.
2. **AN INFERENCE HAZARD THE FILE'S OWN LAYOUT MANUFACTURES.** The header at line 8 records Cox distinguishing Zinn from *"the person of interest then in custody"* — a man the transcript leaves unnamed. §1.3 then supplies a name for a second detainee. 3. **STEELMAN, CONSIDERED AND REJECTED.** The strongest case for keeping is research utility. Research utility is not a public question, and the argument fails on its own terms: both citations remain in place and contain the name, so retrievability is untouched — confirmed against the slug check, which found the removal is not silently undone by its own footnotes.

## PART V — 🚨 PAIRED EDITS: APPLYING ONE HALF IS WORSE THAN APPLYING NEITHER

**P1 — §2.1 text trim (A1 + A2 + B6) ↔ the Breitbart citation line at line 80.**
The slug check is not sufficient here and this is the defect it does not catch. The citation reads *"Breitbart (charging-document detail; corroborated on core facts by T3 outlets)"* — its **sole function in §2.1 is to support the charging-document detail A1 removes**, and its own parenthetical label points at the removed content. Trimming the text and leaving the citation reproduces the fa26905 defect in its exact form: a footnote pointing at what the file just removed. Removing the citation without the text strips a source from a claim that still stands. **Drop the Breitbart line from §2.1 only; it remains cited at §3.2 for the sentence, so the source is not concealed, merely no longer pointed at removed material.** Replacement source list is in the A1/A2 block.

**P2 — §1.3 name removal ↔ [T2] → [T3] tier correction ↔ the Q-40 boundary note.**
Name removed but **[T2]** left = an inflated tier now attached to a proposition whose only support is T3, and an open invitation to a future editor to "restore" the name as though Tier 2 backed it. Tier corrected but name left = the exposure remains *and* the file now advertises that the name rests on weaker sourcing than claimed. The boundary note is what stops the removal from being undone by inference in the other direction. **All three move together or none do.**

**P3 — §4.3 "mental-instability" trim ↔ §4.5 competency paragraph ↔ the new §4.5 pointer.**
The pointer is what converts §4.5 from an isolated court fact into the file's stated guardrail. **Standing constraint:** §4.5 must not be removed in any later pass while B2 is applied — trimming the diagnostic language and then losing the paragraph that records *no competency finding exists* would leave the speculation standing with nothing to check it.

**P4 — §2.2 theft-case amendment ↔ roadmap target A9 (cross-file).**
If an editor overrides C3 and **drops** the sentence instead of amending it, `t1 source acquisition roadmap - George Zinn.md` target **A9** and the "step zero" three-matters enumeration are orphaned and must be re-anchored or removed in the same edit. The amendment path has no such dependency, which is a further reason to prefer it.

**P5 — §4.3 offence-catalogue trim ↔ retention of the Gill characterisation (directional).**
The catalogue is the context reading toward chronic minor offending; Gill's assessment reads toward harmlessness and cuts **against** the payment claim. Removing the catalogue while keeping Gill leaves a net edit that is mildly favourable to Zinn, which is acceptable because the pattern claim survives intact and still carries the self-generated hypothesis. **Removing both, or removing Gill alone, would be one-directional and is forbidden without revisiting B3.**

**P6 — Every applied edit ↔ a revision-log row and a version bump.** The file has no revision log at all (C5). Create the table and open it with:


WHAT SURVIVES (verified by direct reading, speakers inferred from CONTENT not labels):
1. The Mason quote is verbatim at line 19 of ".../2026-08-16_rev_press-conference-on-charlie-kirk-shooting.txt". Speaker confirmed by content self-identification, not the Rev label: "Hello, everyone. 2. The §1.7 text is quoted accurately (zinn-george-evidence.md line 61).
3. A facial tension between them is real — but it is NOT new. It is already recorded, verified and deliberately left unresolved at "files - George Zinn/ZINN-REVIEW-2026-08-17_partial-reconciliation.md" §2 (lines 36-47), which itself names the two-senses reading and labels it an inference. The finding's only new content is the counter-anchor.

WHY THE COUNTER-ANCHOR FAILS — the cited source says the opposite:
(a) day3.txt:1331 and 1339 (Brian Davis, sworn T1). Read AROUND the quote and it separates the two senses rather than merging them: Robinson "arrived at the Utah County Jail about 7:00 AM on the 12th... And he was formally booked in at about 8:00 AM of that morning" — physical arrival and booking are ONE HOUR APART. Davis then defines booking as pure paperwork: "I filled out the necessary paperwork essentially with the jail, which gives the individual's personal identification of the charges, the probable cause statement, and then it's signed and submitted to the system." Sworn testimony therefore ESTABLISHES that booking is a documentary act distinct from physical intake — precisely the distinction the finding claims the corpus refutes.
(b) Cox has zero discriminating power. He spoke on the morning of 2025-09-12, after "the president this morning" report — by which time BOTH the physical intake and the paperwork booking were complete for Robinson. A usage instance in which both candidate senses are simultaneously true cannot adjudicate between them. He was also answering "where he is right now?" — a location question — so the phrasing is driven by the question, not by a technical choice of sense. I could not fix the presser's absolute clock from the corpus (relative timestamps only; "Good morning"/"this morning" are the only markers), but the anchor fails under BOTH timings: if after 8:00 AM it cannot discriminate; if before, it actively demonstrates loose non-physical usage.
(c) Speaker mismatch. The word at issue is MASON's. Cox is the Governor, a different speaker; one man's loose locational usage is not a usage rule for another.
(d) Positive corpus evidence FOR the two-senses reading, unmentioned by the finding. Utah County Attorney Jeff Gray's 2025-09-13 statement, reproduced inside dkt250 (".../2025-12-17_defendant-motion-disqualify-utah-county-attorneys-office_dkt250_dc27880873.txt", lines 523/558/560), uses booking expressly as charge-lodging: booked "on suspicion of" three crimes; "the preliminary charges that supported Mr. Robinson's booking into jail"; "the charges on which Mr. Robinson was booked, and the formal charges we plan to file on Tuesday." And the PC affidavit (dc27880530, lines 128-137) carries booking as record metadata — "Booking Agency: Utah County Sheriff Office", "Booking Agency ORI: UT0250000", Agency Inmate ID, "Probable Cause Entered: 09/12/2025 07:18", officer "UTBDAVIS - Brian Davis", and "Arrest Date/Time: NONE". A booking record with an agency field and a null arrest time is an administrative artifact.
(e) Mason's own locution is agency-shaped in exactly that way — booked "BY Utah Valley University Police Department," naming a booking agency, matching the paperwork structure. He never says Zinn physically entered a jail and never mentions a hospital; "released from custody" is compatible with release to a hospital. The primary source does not, on its face, assert the thing §1.7 would contradict.

Since the second conjunct is not merely overstated but inverted, and acting on it would wrongly move the library toward resolving against §1.7, the compound finding is false as stated.

METHOD / RESIDUAL SCOPE: Excluded the contaminated BAM Franchising file (dc28417731) from all sweeps and separately confirmed it holds zero book* hits, so it was not injecting false hits here either way. Ran the book* sweep under BOTH U+FFFE readings via artifact_search.py (join=True and join=False) across 71 artifacts — 21 hits under each, identical, so no split-form "booked"/"booking" is hidden from either reading; the pattern "book(ed|ing)" is capable of matching the thing at issue. RELEVANT PATHS: ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - George Zinn/zinn-george-evidence.md (§1.7, line 61); ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - George Zinn/ZINN-REVIEW-2026-08-17_partial-reconciliation.md (§2, lines 36-47); ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2026-08-16_rev_press-conference-on-charlie-kirk-shooting.txt (line 19); .../prelim-hearing-transcripts/day3.txt (lines 1331-1341); .../2025-12-17_defendant-motion-disqualify-utah-county-attorneys-office_dkt250_dc27880873.txt (lines 523, 558-560); .../2025-09-16_affidavit-of-probable-cause_dc27880530.txt (lines 128-137).

REFUTED on its load-bearing half. The finding has two components; the first is real but not new, and the second — the "counter-anchor," the only new thing the finding offers — collapses when the cited testimony is read past the sentence the finding stopped at.

1) THE CONFLICT IS REAL BUT ALREADY BANKED; the finding's "File says" framing misstates the file's current state. §1.7 does read exactly as quoted (verified verbatim, line 61 of ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - George Zinn/zinn-george-evidence.md). But the file is not unaware: its own header banner (lines 8-12, added 2026-08-17) says "🚨 §1.7 IS IN CONFLICT WITH THAT SOURCE," quotes Mason's "has been booked into the county jail by Utah Valley University Police Department," labels the two-senses reading "an inference, not a finding," and instructs "Do not cite §1.7's booking date without this caveat." The evidence file also already cross-references "Robinson arrest/booking time conflicts" at line 168. The contradiction half adds nothing.

2) THE COUNTER-ANCHOR FAILS, AND THE SOURCE IT CITES CUTS THE OTHER WAY. The finding quotes day3 and stops one question short of the definition that destroys it. Full passage (.../prelim-hearing-transcripts/day3.txt, ~46:49-47:05; speaker inferred from content, not the Rev label — the witness self-identifies, "And then I was the booking officer"): "We arrived at the Utah County Jail about 7:00 AM on the 12th, September 12th. And he was formally booked in at about 8:00 AM of that morning. And then I was the booking officer. / Q: What does it mean to be the booking officer? / A: I filled out the necessary paperwork essentially with the jail, which gives the individual's personal identification of the charges, the probable cause statement, and then it's signed and submitted to the system." That is Tier 1 sworn testimony establishing (a) that physical arrival (7:00) and being "formally booked in" (8:00) are distinct events an hour apart, and (b) that the booking act is defined as paperwork lodging charges and the PC statement. The cited anchor supports the two-senses reading it was offered to refute.

The 09-12 press conference is content-dated to the morning of 2025-09-12 ("Good morning"; "On the evening of September 11th"; "You heard the president this morning") — after both the 7:00 arrival and the 8:00 formal booking. When Cox said "right now, Mr. Robinson has been booked into the Utah County Jail," both candidate senses were simultaneously satisfied. A usage instance in which both readings are true cannot be evidence against either. On the only alternative branch — a presser before 8:00 AM — Cox's "has been booked" would have preceded formal booking, favouring loose usage even more strongly. Both branches defeat the anchor. It is also the wrong construction: Mason's is agency-action framing, "booked into the county jail BY Utah Valley University Police Department," an administrative act attributed to an agency; Cox's names no actor. One instance by a different speaker two days later cannot fix another speaker's sense, and showing the phrase is used when the person is physically present does not show it is used only then.

4) CORPUS USAGE RUNS AGAINST THE ANCHOR TOO. Sweeping all 71 banked artifacts for book/books/booked/booking under BOTH U+FFFE readings via artifact_search.find, EXCLUDING the mis-banked BAM Franchising file 2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt (excluded, and I say so): dkt250 (2025-12-17 disqualification motion) quotes the county attorney tying booking to charges rather than to a body in a building — "arrested and booked into the Utah County Jail early Friday morning on suspicion of committing three crimes," "the charges on which Mr. Robinson was booked," "the preliminary charges that supported Mr. Robinson's booking into jail." The 2025-09-16 probable-cause affidavit's submission block carries "Arrest Date/Time: NONE" and a 09/12/2025 07:18 timestamp whose field label cannot be reliably paired because the extraction scrambled the two-column layout — so it cannot be used in either direction, and I do not use it. Nothing in the corpus shows the charges-lodged sense is unavailable.

5) MASON'S OWN SENTENCE IS INTERNALLY LOOSE. "He was released from custody after we identified that he did not match the shooting suspect... However, he has been booked into the county jail" — released and booked in adjacent clauses, at a live same-day presser hours after the shot. On its face that cannot bear a precise custody-location reading, and the same file's §1.5-1.6 place Zinn at Utah Valley Regional Medical Center that afternoon speaking with FBI and Utah SBI agents.

Pressing the counter-anchor would resolve, by inference, that Zinn — a living person, cleared on the record of any connection to the shooting — was physically jailed on 2025-09-10 rather than hospitalised. That is an analyst-layer assertion about a third party's custody status derived from a different speaker describing a different person: the cardinal error this project names. It would also resolve against the T3 reporting (booked 09-15, held without bail 09-15) without steelmanning it and without the Tier 1 record that would settle it.

7) Q-40: NOT CROSSED. In fairness, the finding does not merge Zinn with CR-E04 §5.4's early detainee and does not infer identity from partial information. Mason names Zinn himself; Cox's "That is not George Zinn" is not invoked as an identification. The gate holds.

8) MINOR RECORDING-LAYER SLIP. The finding renders the testimony as "[he] arrived at the Utah County Jail about 7:00 AM." The witness said "WE arrived" — the transport team, not Robinson alone. The bracket presents a subject substitution as a pronoun clarification.

SEARCH-NULL DISCIPLINE: no null is asserted. Every search ran through artifact_search.find, which tests both the join and hyphen readings of U+FFFE; the patterns used (\bbook|books|booked|booking\b, "Zinn", "book") are each capable of matching the thing at issue. reasons:
REFUTED AS A CONTRADICTION, though its quotations and its speaker inference are accurate. Three failures, one of them a hard-gate crossing.

(1) 🚨 Q-40 GATE CROSSED — the load-bearing failure. The passage names NOBODY. Across day1.txt the detainee is only "a suspect," "someone," "the person," "he." I searched a pattern capable of matching the thing claimed: "Zinn" returns 0 hits in day1/day2/day3/day4/day5.txt, and "Qureshi" (the second detainee named at the file's §1.3) also returns 0 across all five. Per the standing structural fact, that null is EXPECTED — Zinn was prosecuted separately and is not in Robinson's docket No. 251403576 — so it is not a finding about the world; it simply means this transcript cannot identify the detainee. The finding's operative clause, "earlier and more located than the file's ~2-minute account," is only meaningful if the courtyard detainee IS Zinn. That identity is precisely what Q-40 forbids assuming, and ZINN-REVIEW-2026-08-17 §66 says so in terms: "At least two people were detained on 2025-09-10, and the temptation to merge them is exactly what Q-40 exists to prevent. Do not." A contradiction requires both statements to be about the same subject; here that is unestablished, so no contradiction is available. (For completeness on the steelman: the 2025-09-10 presser does place Zinn "in custody shortly after the shooting" per Commissioner Beau Mason, which makes the merge tempting — but Mason's phrase is not a 30-second anchor, and Cox's "That is not George Zinn" distinguishes Zinn from a LATER person of interest, not from this one. Tempting is not established.)

(2) THE FINDING MIS-DESCRIBES ITS OWN TARGET. §1.1's "approximately two minutes" times Zinn BEGINNING TO SHOUT that he was the shooter — not a detention. §1.2's detention is consequent on those "persistent claims," i.e. later still. So even if identity were granted, "~30 seconds" and "~2 minutes" are not the same measurement, and the file's account of the detention time is simply absent rather than contradicted.

(3) HEARSAY-INSIDE-TESTIMONY PROMOTED TO OBSERVED FACT. Bagley witnessed no detention — he was descending the Hall of Flags stairs ("trying to get down the stairs, jumping over people"). The 30 seconds answers "how long ... did you HEAR that?", and is hedged: "Within 30 seconds maybe." His direct-examination version (3129) carries no time figure at all: "By the time I got to the bottom of the stairs, I was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody." The location is expressly flagged as belief by counsel herself at 5358 — "At that time, it was your UNDERSTANDING the person they took into custody was close by Mr. Kirk" — and his own words are hedged, "somewhere down there." "Courtyard" is counsel's word, supplied in a leading question (5322) that also conflates where the person WAS AT THE SHOOTING with where the detention OCCURRED. "Sworn T1 puts a courtyard detention ~30 seconds after the shot, beside Kirk's tent" therefore states as analyst-layer fact what the record carries only as one officer's recollection of radio traffic. T1 as to what Bagley said; nothing more as to the fact, time or place of any detention.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT NEW. The speaker claim is fully verified independently: Novak is defence counsel (appearances at day1.txt 232, "Kathy Nestor, Michael Burt, Richard Novak, and Stacy Visser here on behalf of Mr. Robinson"; and 448, "Richard Novak for Mr. Robinson"), yet every witness answer from 641 onward carries his label — including the oath response and the self-identification at 672, "Christopher Bagley. Last name spelling B-A-G-L-E-Y." Bagley holds the stand from 628 until Hull is called at 6299, so line 5314 is inside his cross. But CR-E05 §1.2 already banks this and it is QUEUE.md standing hazard 9; CR-E05 line 204 already banks the substance too ("The wrong person was detained. Someone was taken into custody within ~30 seconds, 'right down by where Charlie Kirk was sitting by his tent'"). So the finding presents as new what the library recorded on 2026-07-28.

TWO NUMERIC CLAIMS IN THE FINDING ARE WRONG, both by exactly 2x. "Bagley" occurs 25 times in day1.txt (finding says 50) — identical count in day1_raw.html, so not an extraction artifact — and 6 times in 2026-08-11_defendant-prelim-hearing-briefing.txt (finding says 12), also 6 in the ALT-EXTRACTION-dc28551955 copy. 0 occurrences in day2-day5.

Method notes: I read day1.txt 5220-5560 and 626-760 in full rather than grepping the quote; I checked every witness transition (628 Bagley in, 6275 excused, 6299 Hull called) to confirm no witness swap between cross-onset at 4718 and the passage. I did not use the FFFE-affected artifacts folder search here — day1.txt is not in the affected set and the quoted strings matched directly — and the mis-banked BAM Franchising file (2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt) was never in scope, since all searches were confined to the five hearing-day transcripts and named files. NOT RE-VERIFIED: whether any other artifact in the library independently times Zinn's detention; whether CR-E04 §5.4's detainee is the same person as this one (that is Q-40 itself and remains open); and CR-E05's own internal inconsistency between "within roughly a minute" (line 150) and "~30 seconds" (line 204), which I noticed but did not adjudicate.

REFUTED as framed — it is typed a "contradiction" of the Zinn file, and that framing requires an identification the record does not make and this library expressly forbids.

**1. The transcript names nobody, and the finding supplies the name.** Bagley's cross (day1.txt 5302–5370) says "a suspect," "someone," "the person," "him." It never says Zinn. Searched with `artifact_search.find()` under BOTH readings of the U+FFFE split (join and hyphen), over all 71 banked `.txt` artifacts **excluding the mis-banked BAM Franchising complaint** (`2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt`): `zinn` returns **zero** in day1.txt and hits in exactly one artifact of 71 — the same-day press conference. `george` returns zero in day1.txt; every "George" in the transcript corpus is **St. George**, the city (day3/day4/briefing, all inspected, not counted). Patterns capable of matching the thing claimed: `zinn` and `george` are the man's own name. Per the standing bound, that null is EXPECTED — Zinn was prosecuted separately and is not in the Robinson docket — so it is a fact about the corpus, not about him. But it is fatal to a finding that needs the detainee to be him.

**2. The record cuts against the identification, not toward it.** (a) The file's own §1.3 records **two** people detained 2025-09-10, both cleared. (b) Bagley's detainee was believed to **be the shooter** — "he was in custody with the prisoner of the shooter," "I thought that was him" — whereas CR-E04 §5.4's early detainee was expressly "**not considered to be a suspect**." Different informational states; merging them is precisely what Q-40 exists to prevent. (c) Cox's "That is not George Zinn" distinguishes Zinn from the person of interest in custody later that day. **Q-40 gate crossed.**

**3. The two timings are not the same fact, so they cannot contradict.** §1.1's "approximately two minutes" times when Zinn **began to shout** he was the shooter — not a detention. §1.2, the detention paragraph, carries **no time at all** (verified: the only `\bminutes?\b` in the whole file is §1.1's; every `\bseconds?\b` is "second-degree felony"). So there is no "~2-minute account" of a detention for the transcript to be "earlier" than. The finding manufactures the conflict by transposing §1.1's shouting time onto §1.2's untimed detention and attaching both to an unnamed man. If anything the arithmetic **reverses** the finding: a man already in custody at ~30 s cannot easily be a man who only started shouting at ~2 min and was detained *because of* those persistent claims (§1.2) — which makes the timing a reason to **doubt** the identification.

**4. The witness is not percipient to the detention.** Bagley was on the Hall of Flags walkway and then "jumping over people" on the stairs; his custody knowledge is a **radio transmission** — sworn testimony as to what he heard, hearsay as to who was detained and where. His own location answer is hedged ("somewhere down there"), and "in the courtyard area at the time of the shooting" is **Nester's leading formulation** assented to with a bare "Yes." He later testified he "realized that we probably didn't have our shooter in custody" (day1.txt 4398). T1 as to what Bagley said; not T1 as to the fact.

**5. Not new — and the library's banked version is already the correct one.** `CR-E05_prelim-hearing-Day1_Bagley-Hull-first-tranche.md` §3 already records this exact passage: "**The wrong person was detained.** Someone was taken into custody within ~30 seconds, 'right down by where Charlie Kirk was sitting by his tent' — in the courtyard, not near the holster." reasons:
REFUTED as a compound. The core null survives, but two stated limbs fail — one against the face of the cited source, one against the project's own scope rule.

WHAT SURVIVES. I fetched https://www.unz.com/article/george-zinn-a-deep-dive-into-the-facts/ (retrieved 2026-08-17). Byline "Greg Garros", displayed date January 29, 2026, both quoted sentences verbatim. The piece supplies no hospital record, no named staff member, no recording and no document, and expressly says the claim "has yet to be proven." I independently re-measured the corpus: across all 71 banked .txt artifacts, BAM Franchising complaint excluded, under BOTH U+FFFE readings via artifact_search.find, the stem `nurs` returns ZERO — a pattern capable of matching the thing claimed absent. `Zinn` = 3 occurrences in 1 artifact (the same-day press conference). Every `hospital`/`doctor` hit concerns Kirk's transport to Timpanogos Regional and the medical examiner's autopsy (day1, Agent David Hull); the only `reward` is the FBI's $100,000 tip reward. No news-organization corroboration found in searches to 2026-08-17. So: nothing corroborates or refutes the claim, and it remains Tier 4 and uncorroborated.

FAILURE 1 — the source does NOT attribute the claim solely to Owens. Reading around the quote, the article embeds an X post by a named third party, Evan Kilgore (@EvanAKilgore, status 1975695531432194168; snowflake decodes to 2025-10-07T22:51:35Z), asserting in his own voice that "George Zinn told medical staff he was 'getting paid' to claim he was the shooter, but wasn't sure from who or when." It sits inside a passage arguing the story "has been commented on by millions of Americans... including many social media influencers, alternative investigators, podcasters, and public figures." A second named propagator is present in the very artifact the finding characterises as attributing "SOLELY to Owens." The conclusion still holds — Kilgore adds no record, no named staff member, no recording, no document, and his 2025-10-07 post postdates Owens' September 2025 broadcasts, so §5.1's origin finding stands — but the finding states a property of the source that the source contradicts.

FAILURE 2 — the null CANNOT be "widened to the sworn record." The only sworn record the library holds is the ROBINSON preliminary hearing (day1–day5) plus Robinson's charging papers. I checked the banked `2025-09-16_affidavit-of-probable-cause_dc27880530.txt` and `2025-09-16_information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt`: both are captioned ROBINSON, TYLER JAMES. They are NOT the Dutson Zinn affidavit that §5.2 refers to. Zinn was prosecuted separately; he is not a party or a witness in No. 251403576, and hospital-staff statements about him would never appear in that record. Widening there imports a search space that would not necessarily contain the claim — an expected null dressed as coverage, forbidden by objectivity mechanic 3 — and invites the affidavit conflation of announcing "the affidavit, now read directly" when the affidavit read directly belongs to a different defendant. Zinn's affidavit, plea and sentencing record remain unheld and remain "as reported."

TWO FURTHER SOURCE-LENS DEFECTS. (i) The finding calls the Substack a "twin"; the direction is inverted — Unz carries "Republished from Substack by permission of author or representative," so Substack is the original and Unz the republication. Their displayed dates conflict (Unz January 29, 2026; Substack January 30, 2026) and cannot both be right given the republication direction; the Substack slug `george-zinn-the-basic-facts` against the title "A Deep Dive Into the Facts" also indicates a retitle. Flag, do not smooth. (ii) The finding truncates the quotation at a comma. The sentence continues: "...but if it is true, it certainly suggests Zinn may have been involved in or used in some type of organized assassination plot against Kirk." The omitted clause pivots the source from self-limiting to conditionally inferential, which is material to how the piece is characterised in the recording layer.

RECORDING-LAYER DRIFT WORTH REGISTERING. Three variants now circulate: Garros writes "promised payment" to "nurses and doctors"; Kilgore writes "getting paid... wasn't sure from who or when"; §5.1 records Owens as "was paid... did not know the source of the money." A promise of payment and a receipt of payment are different claims with different corroboration paths, and §5.4's register label "PAID FALSE CONFESSION" fixes only one variant. Garros, Unz and Kilgore appear nowhere in the library — the entire propagation layer is unrecorded, which is a completeness gap in §5.1, not a defect in §5.2's null.

STANDING GATES OBSERVED. Zinn is a living person, cleared on the record by named officials of any connection to the shooting; nothing above implies otherwise. Q-40 untouched — this work does not bear on whether CR-E04 §5.4's early detainee is Zinn, and I did not assume it. No detail about the exploitation material was retrieved, reproduced or searched for.

RESIDUAL SCOPE. I did not re-verify §5.1's Shawn Ryan Show or Owens X citations, did not open the Kilgore post itself (text taken from the Substack rendering of the embed), did not resolve the Unz/Substack date conflict, and did not re-test D3. My corpus null is a fact about the library's holdings only, and those holdings do not include Zinn's case.

The finding is compound, and its operative half is wrong. Part (a) survives; the prescription "widen to the sworn record" does not, and executing it would put a defect into the file.

WHAT SURVIVES. §5.2's corroboration null holds. I verified the Unz piece by direct retrieval (Greg Garros, The Unz Review, 2026-01-29) and its Substack twin (ggarros1.substack.com, 2026-01-30). Both attribute the claim solely to Owens, cite no named hospital staff member, no hospital record, no recording and no document, and both say in terms "This particular claim has yet to be proven." Both predate the file's 2026-07-13 null, so neither disturbs it; the finding's characterisation of them is accurate. Four web queries on 2026-08-17 surfaced only further propagation (a Facebook repost), not corroboration. ⚠️ But the re-dating to 2026-08-17 rests on those four queries plus a corpus sweep — NOT an outlet-by-outlet survey. A dated null is a claim about the world on a date and must state its method; as phrased it reads as a completed currency survey it was not.

WHY THE WIDENING IS REFUTED, NOT MERELY TRIMMED.

1. The sworn record is structurally incapable of carrying this null. Zinn was prosecuted separately and is not a party to No. 251403576. Measured 2026-08-17 across all 71 banked artifacts (the mis-banked BAM Franchising v. "Reckless Ben" complaint EXCLUDED, and every pattern run under BOTH U+FFFE readings via artifact_search.find): \bzinn\b → 1 file, 3 occurrences, all in the 2025-09-10 press-conference transcript, which is Tier 2 and NOT sworn; zero in every banked filing and in all five preliminary-hearing days. Patterns capable of matching the thing claimed absent — nurs\w*, brib\w*, compensat\w*, "false confession|fake confession", "promised pay\w*" — return ZERO across all 71 under both readings. Every \bpaid\b hit is a witness-fee/docket-cost context (Hull subpoena, XChange case history); every pay/paying hit in the sworn transcripts is Rev boilerplate ("Pay-Per-Minute Services"), "pay attention", "pay the fee", or "above my pay grade"; every hospital* hit in the sworn filings and Day 1 is Kirk's transport to Timpanogos Regional, not Zinn's. Under the project's own rule (objectivity mechanic 3), absence is evidence of absence only if the search space would necessarily contain the record. It would not. Widening §5.2 to the sworn record converts an EXPECTED corpus fact into apparent evidentiary weight about a living person in a homicide investigation — the precise error the task brief names.

refuted.label: (b) D3's Jan 28 vs Jan 29 conflict is NOT settled — three primary retrievals failed, and D3 itself contains a small mis-attribution about which outlet's caption says what
reasons:
REFUTED on its operative new claim. The finding has two conjuncts. Conjunct 1 ("not settled") is true but adds nothing — D3 already says in terms "flagged, not resolved. Resolution path: 4th District Court docket," so confirming it restates the file. Conjunct 2 — that "D3 itself contains a small mis-attribution about which outlet's caption says what" — is affirmatively contradicted by the sources.

D3's sentence under attack reads: "Salt Lake Tribune photo captions conflict internally: some (syndicated in Deseret/ABC4 pieces) date the arraignment 'Wednesday, Jan. 28, 2026'; the Tribune's own sentencing article captions it 'Thursday, Jan. 29, 2026.'" I checked every outlet D3 names. The finding checked only two of the three and stopped at the one where the credit line is ambiguous.

ABC4 is decisive and the finding never retrieved it. abc4.com returns HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl (access-path caveat), so I read the Wayback snapshot captured 2026-01-30 (web.archive.org/web/20260130085736/…). Its captions read VERBATIM, credit line included: "(Bethany Baker | The Salt Lake Tribune) George Zinn appears at his arraignment where he entered a no-contest plea to an obstruction of justice charge after police say he falsely claimed that he had shot Charlie Kirk, at Fourth District Court in Provo on Wednesday, Jan. 28, 2026." Four such captions, each carrying the Tribune's own credit format, each dating the hearing Jan. 28. The Tribune's own page carries the identical credit format and says Thursday, Jan. 29 ("Jan. 28" appears zero times on sltrib.com; "Jan. 29" nine times, in two captions plus image JSON). That is exactly the internal conflict within Tribune-credited caption material that D3 described. D3's attribution is correct as written.

Deseret independently confirms the syndication D3 asserted, contrary to the finding's implicit reading that the Jan. 28 caption is Deseret's own. Deseret's VISIBLE credit is only "| Bethany Baker" — which is presumably what led the finding astray, and the finding's "verbatim" Deseret quote drops even that credit tail, the one element in dispute. But Deseret's embedded image objects carry "copyright":"© 2026 Bethany Baker | The Salt Lake Tribune", "takenOn":"2026-01-29T00:00:00Z", and slugs 260129_ZINNARRAIGNMENT.013026_1052_bb.jpg / _1073_bb.jpg — the same photographer, same shoot, same file slugs ABC4 published under the explicit Tribune credit. Deseret's own staff photos on the same page read "| Tess Crowley, Deseret News" and "| Jeffrey D. Allred, Deseret News", so the Baker images are visibly not Deseret-originated.

What the finding got right and I confirmed at source: Deseret published 2026-01-29 4:31 p.m. MST, updated 2026-01-30 9:43 a.m. MST, byline Eva Terry, caption text as quoted (minus the dropped credit); Tribune caption as quoted, though truncated without ellipsis — it continues "Zinn pleaded no contest to an obstruction of justice charge amid the Charlie Kirk shooting, and pleaded guilty to two counts of sexual exploitation of a minor."; KSL posted Jan. 29, 2026 3:06 p.m., caption "George Zinn appears in court Thursday… (Bethany Baker)" and body "Thursday," with no calendar date in either — "Jan. 28" appears nowhere on KSL. D3's further claims also hold: Deseret body says "Thursday" three times and never "Jan. 29"; ABC4 body says "pleaded guilty Thursday"; Jan. 29, 2026 was a Thursday and Jan. 28 a Wednesday (so the bad caption is an internally consistent one-day-early error, not a day/date mismatch).

Two further notes. (1) The cited sources cannot carry the "three primary retrievals failed" clause — all three URLs are Tier 3 news, none is a primary retrieval; that clause is a claim about this project's own access attempts and stands or falls elsewhere, not on these sources. (2) A Yahoo mirror of the Deseret piece returned a fetch-model artifact asserting the body says "Wednesday, Jan. 28, 2026"; the Deseret HTML shows no such body sentence — "Jan. 28" occurs only in captions and image metadata. I did not treat that artifact as evidence.

Net effect on the record: the Jan. 29 reading is now STRONGER than when D3 was written — the Tribune photographer's own file slugs (260129) and Deseret's takenOn field both date the shoot 2026-01-29 — but this is metadata embedded in Tier 3 pages, not a court record, so D3's "flagged, not resolved" posture and its Tier 1 resolution path remain correct and unchanged. No correction to D3's outlet attribution is warranted; making the one the finding proposes would introduce an error where none exists.

REFUTED on its distinctive limb, and the refutation comes from the finding's own cited sources.

1. THERE IS NO MIS-ATTRIBUTION IN D3. Retrieved 2026-08-17: the Deseret News piece carries FOUR captioned photos. The two Zinn arraignment photos — both reading "Wednesday, Jan. 28, 2026" — are credited "Bethany Baker" and "| Bethany Baker", with NO outlet tag. The two other photos in the same article are credited "| Tess Crowley, Deseret News" and "| Jeffrey D. Allred, Deseret News". The Salt Lake Tribune's caption reads "(Bethany Baker | The Salt Lake Tribune) ... on Thursday, Jan. 29, 2026." KSL's Zinn courtroom photo is credited "(Bethany Baker)". So one Salt Lake Tribune photographer's images of this hearing ran in all three outlets, and the Jan-28 captions sit on Tribune photography carried in the Deseret piece — which is exactly what D3 says: "Salt Lake Tribune photo captions conflict internally: some (syndicated in Deseret/ABC4 pieces) date the arraignment 'Wednesday, Jan. 28, 2026'; the Tribune's own ... article captions it 'Thursday, Jan. 29, 2026.'" D3 is correct as written.

2. HOW THE FINDING MANUFACTURED THE ERROR: asymmetric quotation. It reproduced the Tribune caption WITH its "(Bethany Baker | The Salt Lake Tribune)" credit and the Deseret caption WITHOUT its trailing "Bethany Baker" credit — deleting the one element on the face of the artifact that decides whose caption it is. The credit line is content, not decoration.

3. STAKES — the finding fails its own lens. Acting on it would have moved a documented date error OFF the Salt Lake Tribune and ONTO the Deseret News, i.e. it claims more about a named third party (an outlet, and by implication a named photographer's caption set) than the source carries, committing the precise defect it alleges. Clean on the two hard gates: it never touches the early-detainee identification, so NO Q-40 crossing; it reproduces no child-victim detail; and it asserts nothing about Mr. Zinn beyond recording-layer caption text consistent with the file's §3.1.

4. "THREE PRIMARY RETRIEVALS FAILED" IS UNSUPPORTED AS STATED. The three URLs it cites are all Tier 3 news and ALL THREE retrieved successfully on re-test 2026-08-17. The only failure I reproduced is abc4.com HTTP 403 — a standing bot-block already logged in DOCKET-WATCH-routine-prompt-DRAFT-2026-08-14, and not a primary source; it leaves D3's ABC4 leg untested, not falsified. The genuine primary route — Zinn's Fourth District docket via Utah XChange — is paywalled and owner-gated (QUEUE Q-31, START-HERE Q-149) and was never attempted: BLOCKED, not failed. The project rule requires a failure count to name its routes; this one names none.

5. WHAT SURVIVES is only the trivial half, which the file already states itself ("flagged, not resolved. Resolution path: 4th District Court docket"). The library's own Tier 1 holdings cannot close it: searched 165 artifacts excluding the mis-banked BAM Franchising file (2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt), BOTH readings via artifact_search.py, plus a Python read of the XChange docket files per Hazard 13 (grep is void there). Patterns were capable — "Zinn" returns 44 corpus-wide, "January 28"/"January 29" return 6/20 — yet every Jan 28/29 docket entry is a ROBINSON filing (media-access and classification motions, No. 251403576) with zero "Zinn" and zero "arraign". EXPECTED: Zinn was prosecuted separately, so his docket is not in this corpus at all. That is a fact about the corpus, not about Mr. Zinn.

6. VERIFYING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the retrieval STRENGTHENS D3 rather than weakening it. Deseret's own body says "Thursday in Utah's 4th District Court, Zinn pleaded no contest ..." against its own "Wednesday, Jan. 28" captions, published 2026-01-29 4:31 p.m. MST; KSL published 2026-01-29 3:06 p.m. saying "Thursday". Two same-day publications place the hearing on Thursday, Jan. 29 — D3's stated best-supported reading.

7. ONE REAL GAP BOTH D3 AND THE FINDING MISS, and it is better ground for keeping D3 open than anything the finding offered: verified by calendar, Jan 28 2026 WAS a Wednesday and Jan 29 WAS a Thursday, so each disputed caption pairs weekday and date correctly and neither is a self-inconsistent typo. D3's "likely caption errors" is therefore softer than it reads, and a two-proceedings reading (arraignment one day, sentencing the next) is not excluded by anything retrieved — though it draws no support from Deseret, whose body and caption place the same no-contest plea on different days. Note also that the Tribune page shows no publication timestamp; its date comes from the URL slug, which is metadata, not content.

## (a) HELD SOURCES NO READER OPENED

Verified by listing both folders and diffing against every source cited in the surviving and refuted findings.

**A1. `2025-09-10_utah-county-attorney-press-release-uvu-shooting-investigation_dc27880543.txt` — a same-day, named-official (T2) statement, never opened by anyone in this chain.** Jeff Gray, Utah County Attorney, 2025-09-10. It is silent on Zinn, and that silence is *bounded and unremarkable* (it is a charging-authority statement, not a detentions statement) — but the document is load-bearing for the acquisition programme in three ways nobody has used: it establishes the Utah County Attorney's Office as the prosecuting authority coordinating the UVU investigation; it names the PIO channel (Christopher Ballard, cballard@utahcounty.gov) and office address; and it states "Once the investigation is complete, we will carefully review the evidence and decide on the appropriate charges" — i.e. on 2025-09-10 the County Attorney had charged no one, which is a T2 datum bearing directly on the §1.7 booking-date conflict (booking by UVU PD ≠ charging by the County Attorney). **The roadmap's Route B has no prosecutor's-office leg at all.**

**A2. `2026-03-15ca_utah-county-sheriff-office-inmate-custody-booking_dc27880534.txt` (+ `.pdf`) — an actual UCSO inmate-custody booking capture, never opened.** It is Robinson's, and its OCR is badly degraded (788 bytes of garble). ## (b) CLAIMS NO PASS TESTED

Every pass touched §1.1–1.3, §1.6–1.8, §2.1, §5.1–5.2, D3. **Untested:**

**B1. §3.2's sentence numbers are Utah's statutory ranges, not reported outcomes — and no pass noticed.** "Obstruction: 0–5 years · each exploitation count: 1–15 years" are the indeterminate terms fixed by Utah Code 76-3-203(3) and (2) for third- and second-degree felonies; "$25,000" is exactly the statutory fine maximum stack (76-3-301: $10,000 + $10,000 + $5,000). So §3.2, presented as "Imposed at the same hearing," carries **no independently sourced sentencing content except concurrency** — and concurrency is the one variable a judgment-and-commitment order would settle. Roadmap A6 targets that order but the roadmap never says this is the only thing A6 actually buys.

**B2. §1.7's charge string is verifiable at T1 from a document the library already holds, and nobody checked.** §1.7's odd phrase — "obstruction of justice in a capital/first-degree felony case — a second-degree felony" — is the **verbatim Utah court-system charge label**: `76-8-306(2)+(3A) - OBSTRUCTION OF JUSTICE - CAPITAL/FIRST DEGREE FELONY CONDUCT, 2nd Degree Felony` (read directly at `2026-03-15_xchange-short-case-history_dc27880533.txt`; matching Information language at `2025-09-16_information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt`). ## (c) SILENCES THAT ARE THEMSELVES FINDINGS

**C1. The file never states the structural fact that bounds all of its nulls.** It nowhere says that Zinn was prosecuted separately and his record is therefore not in the Robinson docket. Every "no evidence found" in the file is read by a downstream reader as a search of the library — and the library structurally cannot contain it. ZINN-REVIEW §3 says this; the evidence file does not.

## (d) A REAL TIER 1 ACQUISITION PROGRAMME — AND THE VERDICT ON THE ROADMAP

**The court.** Fourth Judicial District Court, Utah County, **137 North Freedom Boulevard, Provo, UT 84601** (confirmed from the held transcript caption) — the same courthouse as Robinson, **different case numbers, different judge (Thomas Low, per T3, untested), different prosecution team.** At least three matters: obstruction; sexual exploitation (filed 2025-09-19); a January 2025 misdemeanor theft case whose court the roadmap **asserts** is Provo Justice Court with no source — Zinn's documented history is Salt Lake–centred, so Salt Lake justice court is at least as likely. Treat A9's court as a hypothesis.

**THE BLOCKER IS WRONG, AND THIS IS THE MOST ACTIONABLE THING IN THIS REPORT.** The roadmap's Route A, its "step zero," and queue item **Q-149** all treat Zinn's docket as gated on the $10 XChange purchase (Q-31, human, unspent since 2026-07-13). **But the library never used XChange to get Robinson's docket.** `CR-ACQ-2026-08-14C` §1 records that the two banked XChange case histories were pulled from the **open DocumentCloud API** (documents 27880531 / 27880533, project 224251, retrieved 2026-08-14) — "no XChange account exists." So the library has a demonstrated, free, working route to Utah court-record output, used it in the same period, and **has never once pointed it at Zinn.** Q-149's framing has held Route A blocked on human spend for five weeks against a route that was open the whole time. Two caveats to carry: the DocumentCloud web UI is bot-gated (Q-32) while the API is not; and a third-party upload is **zero-of-three on filing provenance** — court-system provenance only — so it is the *fast* route, not the *clean* one.

**Also unrecognised: Zinn's case is CLOSED.** Robinson's docket needs re-pulling forever (the banked one has a hard 2026-03-14 ceiling). Zinn's, pulled once, is **permanently complete**. That inverts the cost-benefit the roadmap assumes.
